outputs.L3:
The valve core is designed to reduce manufacturing costs through a simple, easily assembled structure. It includes first and second core cylinder bodies, with the second core cylinder body defining a valve opening on the side opposite the first core cylinder body. A linearly movable shaft extends through both cylinder bodies and supports a valve body configured to open and close the valve opening.

An elastic member biases the movable shaft so that the second core cylinder body is held between the first core cylinder body and the valve body. The first and second core cylinder bodies are further provided with respective cylindrical fitting sections. These fitting sections are rotatably and detachably fitted together without interference. When assembled, the second fitting section contacts a stepped surface formed on the first fitting section, thereby establishing the intended relative position of the two core cylinder bodies while allowing straightforward assembly and disassembly.
outputs.L4:
A low-cost valve core is formed from first and second core cylinder bodies, a valve member that moves linearly within the cylinder bodies, and an elastic biasing member that urges the valve member toward a predetermined position, such as a closed position. Each core cylinder body includes a cylindrical fitting section. The fitting sections are detachably and rotatably coupled so that the two cylinder bodies can be assembled and separated without requiring complicated fastening structures or specialized tools.

The respective fitting sections are configured not to interfere with one another during attachment or removal. As a result, the cylinder bodies can be connected without transmitting excessive rotational force to the valve member or the elastic biasing member. A stepped contact surface establishes the proper axial relationship between the cylinder bodies and provides a stable seating position when assembly is complete. This structure helps ensure accurate alignment of the internal components and consistent movement of the valve member.

During operation, fluid pressure and the force of the elastic biasing member control the linear displacement of the valve member, thereby opening or closing a fluid passage through the valve core. Because the cylinder bodies can rotate relative to one another during fitting, assembly tolerances are easier to accommodate and damage to the internal components is less likely. The detachable construction also permits convenient inspection, cleaning, repair, or replacement of individual parts.

By reducing the number and complexity of machined features and by simplifying both assembly and disassembly, the valve core can be manufactured at lower cost. At the same time, the stepped contact surface and noninterfering separable fittings maintain secure positioning, smooth valve movement, and dependable sealing performance. The resulting design therefore combines economical production and straightforward maintenance with reliable valve operation.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” can mean any book, while “the book” refers to a particular one understood by the speaker and listener.

Although it consists of only three letters, “the” brings clarity and precision to communication. It helps distinguish the familiar from the unknown and the specific from the general. This small word demonstrates how even the simplest elements of language can play an essential role in shaping meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise patent abstract for a low-cost valve core with two separable, rotatably fitted cylindrical core bodies, a spring-biased movable valve member, and a stepped fitting surface.
counterfactuals.output: A low-cost valve core includes first and second cylindrical core bodies separably coupled for relative rotation. A movable valve member is disposed within the core bodies and biased by a spring toward a valve-closing position. A stepped fitting surface between the core bodies provides axial positioning, sealing, and stable rotational engagement while permitting convenient assembly and disassembly. The simplified multipart construction reduces manufacturing and maintenance costs while maintaining reliable valve operation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the construction of a valve core designed to reduce manufacturing costs, including its valve opening, movable shaft and valve body, elastic biasing member, and detachable fitting sections.
counterfactuals.output:
The valve core is constructed from two easily assembled body sections:

- A **valve opening** is formed in the valve-core body.
- A **shaft** extends through the opening and is movable in the axial direction. A **valve body** fixed to the shaft moves into and out of contact with a valve seat around the opening, thereby closing or opening the flow passage.
- An **elastic biasing member**, such as a coil spring, acts between the shaft and the valve-core body to urge the valve body toward the closed position.
- The valve-core body is divided into separate sections provided with complementary **first and second fitting portions**. These portions detachably engage—such as by snap-fitting—so the sections can be assembled without costly threading, caulking, or extensive machining.

This separable, fitted construction simplifies part manufacture and assembly, thereby reducing manufacturing cost.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2
